cohort: The study included 1283 preterm infants born at < 32 weeks of gestation who received umbilical cord management in 26 tertiary referral neonatal intensive care units.
finding: Delayed cord clamping independently decreased the risk of bronchopulmonary dysplasia in infants born at < 32 weeks of gestation with moderate-to-severe respiratory distress, but this benefit was not observed for those born at < 28 weeks of gestation.
gest_age: < 32 weeks of gestation (primary cohort), < 28 weeks of gestation (subgroup)
